reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a supposedly free PancakeSwap sniper bot while claiming it can produce 1 BNB per day. It directs viewers to connect MetaMask, fund the bot with BNB, and activate automated trading, while showing a contract balance and changing wallet balance without independently verifying the promised returns or control of transferred funds. Although the speaker acknowledges that the bot may fail and BNB may not return, the promotion still relies on an unusually easy wealth claim and a funding flow.

today I'm going to show you here how to build, how to make your own Sniper Bot
we're going to need to feed that contract, we're going to need to put liquidity into this SniperBot
we're going to switch here from JavaScript to Inject Web3. that's where it's going to take our wallet
When I click here on this action button, my bot will look for a new liquidity parity

opening.argument: The presentation includes material qualifications that cut against a guaranteed-return reading. The speaker explicitly says the bot will not work every time and that BNB may sometimes not come back. The process is also described as involving transaction fees and a possible delay, so the outcome is presented as conditional and operationally uncertain rather than assured. A careful viewer is therefore given direct risk information before deciding whether to participate. The title's earnings language should be read alongside these express limitations, not treated as a promise that every user will receive the stated amount.

citations.quote: It's not going to work every time. I'll make this very clear to you right here.
Even if sometimes the BNBs don't come back.
It's going to ask us to put a little bit of Gas back here again, this is normal here

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the title as controlling, but the spoken qualifications materially narrow that impression. The speaker does not say returns are certain: he warns that the bot may fail, funds may not come back, fees are required, and processing may take minutes. Those warnings are difficult to reconcile with a characterization based only on an easy, guaranteed wealth claim.

citations.quote: It's not going to work every time. I'll make this very clear to you right here.
It may take two or three minutes before this process happens.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These caveats do not remove the central inducement. The title still says “Earn 1 BNB per day,” while the speaker instructs viewers to put liquidity into the bot and activate it. Saying that losses or delays may occur acknowledges risk but does not establish that the promoted earnings claim is reliable or that transferred funds remain under the viewer's control.

opening.argument: The video's central activity is a technical walkthrough: it explains how to create a contract, select a compiler, connect a wallet environment, and interact with deployed-contract controls. The speaker expressly frames the subject as showing viewers how to build their own bot, and the supplied frames show Solidity source code, compiler controls, deployment controls, and a blockchain explorer. That is consistent with an operational programming demonstration. Showing a workflow and describing what its buttons are intended to do does not by itself certify a successful investment outcome, and the available material does not independently establish one.

citations.quote: today I'm going to show you here how to build, how to make your own Sniper Bot
so we compile this contract that I've just shown you
we're going to switch here from JavaScript to Inject Web3

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies instructions and wallet interaction, but those are expected features of a technical demonstration involving a blockchain contract. It does not show that the video presents a verified result rather than explaining deployment and operation. The reference framing also relies on what the process could imply, while the technical screens themselves show code, compilation, and controls rather than independently proving a promised return.

citations.quote: The contract is ready. Relax. Here's the address.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial format does not make the financial promotion neutral. The instructions culminate in funding and activating the contract, not merely discussing Solidity. The speaker says the bot will buy and sell and return BNB, while the title advertises a daily amount. Code screens and a deployed-contract interface show implementation, but they do not show that the claimed trading mechanism works or that users will recover funds.

Because at that moment it's there. It's ready for us to use it.

opening.argument: The material can be understood as promotion of a software tool and an ordinary implementation service: it provides bot code, identifies development and wallet software, and demonstrates contract deployment and interaction. The supplied record does not show a downline, recruitment scheme, credential request, or a guaranteed payment obligation. Even the operational account includes transaction fees and acknowledges that funds may not return, which is more consistent with a risky software or trading-tool offering than proof of a scam mechanism. The evidence therefore supports classifying the content by its observable technology and service activity, without certifying the tool's safety.

citations.quote: How to make your pancakeswap sniper for free!
Bot code to copy/paste on remix
It's going to ask us to put a little bit of Gas back here again, this is normal here.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening assumes that funding a contract necessarily supplies a scam mechanism, but the record also presents code, deployment, and ordinary network fees. It does not establish recruitment, credential collection, or a guaranteed return. A displayed balance and a contract interaction can document a software demonstration without proving that the creator misappropriates funds or that the tool is incapable of its described function.

citations.quote: So, the contract is already there inside the Binance Smart Chain.
It's going to ask us to put a little bit of Gas back here again, this is normal here.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it a software service does not answer the core concern: viewers are told to fund the contract and activate automated buying and selling in connection with a daily earnings claim. The record need not show recruitment or credential theft for that promotion to be deceptive. The visible balances and transactions demonstrate movement of BNB, but they do not establish profitable trading, control of returned funds, or the advertised outcome.
